name: Review scope

subjectOf.text: A code review should focus on the functionality of the code and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out, rather than on the reviewer imposing their own stylistic logic.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead, a code review should focus on functionality of the code and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How DAOs Optimize Open-Source Code Reviews and Create Open-Source Standards (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3995709

subjectOf.text: A code review should focus on the functionality of the code and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out, rather than on conforming code to a reviewer's stylistic logic.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead, a code review should focus on the functionality of the code and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Code Review DAO (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4734750

subjectOf.text: Without crowd control the reviewer's views and the code author's intent are at odds, so a reviewer imposing their own logic can force repeated rewrites of code whose core functionality is already sound; a code review should instead focus on functionality and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead, a code review should focus on the functionality of the code and on keeping mistaken, badly constructed, and dangerous code out.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632
scope_conditions: applies to legacy code review processes lacking crowd control
